en: Dhātukathā 2:
Niddesa 2.1.
Exposition of the First Method: The Comprehension and Non-comprehension of Categories.
2.1.1. The Aggregate of Form (Rūpakkhandha). By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements is the aggregate of form comprised?
The aggregate of form is comprised by one aggregate, by eleven bases, and by eleven elements.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
By how many aggregates, how many bases, and how many elements is the feeling aggregate included?
The aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha) is included within one aggregate, one base, and one element.
Within how many is it not included?
It is not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements is the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha) comprised?
The aggregate of perception is comprised by one aggregate, by one base, and by one element.
By how many is it not comprised?
It is not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, or seventeen elements.
Within how many aggregates, how many bases, and how many elements is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) included?
The aggregate of volitional formations is included within one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many aggregates, how many bases, and how many elements is the consciousness aggregate included?
The consciousness aggregate (viññāṇakkhandha) is included within one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
Within how many is it not included?
It is not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
(One Rooted.
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are the aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling comprised?
The aggregate of form and the aggregate of feeling are comprised by two aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by three aggregates (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu).
These are the aggregate of form (rūpakkhandha) and the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha) …pe…
They are included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within three aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
The aggregate of form and the aggregate of mental formations … [as above] … are included in two aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included within three aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
The aggregate of form and the aggregate of consciousness … [as above] … are included within two aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by three aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
(The Section Based on Pairs.)
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, and the aggregate of perception comprised?
The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, and the aggregate of perception are comprised by three aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not included in two aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, and the aggregate of mental formations … [as above] … are included in three aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by two aggregates, one base, and seven elements. [Namely:
the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, and the aggregate of consciousness …pe…
They are included within three aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, nor within any bases, nor within any elements.
(With reference to the Triad.

The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are they comprised?
The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations are comprised by four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu).
Namely, the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness …pe…
They are comprised within four aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not uncomprised of any aggregate, nor of any base, nor of any element.
(Section Based on Fourfold Root.

The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are these comprised?

The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness are comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are the five aggregates included?
The five aggregates are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not un-included within any aggregates, nor within any bases, nor within any elements.
(Pentad) 2.1.2.
Bases (Āyatana).
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements is the eye-base (cakkhāyatana) comprised?
The eye-base is included in one aggregate, in one base, and in one element.
In how many is it not included?
It is not included in four aggregates, in eleven bases, and in seventeen elements.

The ear-base … the nose-base … the tongue-base … the body-base … the visible-form base … the sound-base … the odor-base … the flavor-base … the tangible-object base … [and so on] … is comprised by one aggregate, by one base, and by one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
The mind base (*manāyatana*) is included by one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
Excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, the base of mental phenomena (dhammāyatana) is included by four aggregates, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by one aggregate, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
(The section based on the single root.)
The eye-base and the ear-base are included within one aggregate, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The eye base and the nose base; the eye base and the tongue base;
the eye base and the body base; the eye base and the visible-form base;
the eye base and the sound base; the eye base and the odor base; the eye base and the taste base; the eye base and...
The tangible base is included within one aggregate, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many is it not included?
It is not included within four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The eye base and the mind base are included in two aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in three aggregates, ten bases, and ten elements.
Excluding the eye-base and the mental-object-base from the category of the unconditioned, they are comprised by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
(On the Basis of Pairs.
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are the twelve bases comprised?
Excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates, the twelve bases are comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by any elements.
(The group of twelve.)
2.1.3. Elements (Dhātu) The eye-element (cakkhudhātu): by how many aggregates (khandha), by how many bases (āyatana), and by how many elements (dhātu) is it comprised?
The eye-element is comprised by one aggregate, by one base, and by one element.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
[This applies to] the ear element … the nose element … the tongue element … the body element … the visible-form element … the sound element … the odor element.

… the taste element … the tangible-object element … the eye-consciousness element … the ear-consciousness element … the nose-consciousness element … the tongue-consciousness element … the body-consciousness element … the mind-element … the mind-consciousness element are each comprised within one aggregate,
one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
The dhamma-element, setting aside the unconditioned as an aggregate, is included by four aggregates, one base, and one element.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
(The section based on the single root.)
The eye element and the ear element are comprised within one aggregate, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The eye element and the nose element; the eye element and the tongue element; the eye element and the body element;
the eye element and the visible-form element; the eye element and the sound element; the eye element and the odor element;
the eye element and the taste element; the eye element and the tangible-object element.
It is included by one aggregate, two bases, and two elements.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The eye element and the eye-consciousness element are comprised within two aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within three aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.

The eye element and the ear-consciousness element … the eye element and the nose-consciousness element … the eye element and the tongue-consciousness element … the eye element and the body-consciousness element … the eye element and the mind element … the eye element and the mind-consciousness element are included within two aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by three aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The eye element and the mental-object element, setting aside the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
(The section based on pairs.)
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are the eighteen elements comprised?
Excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, the eighteen elements are comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, by any bases, or by any elements.
(The group of eighteen. 2.1.4.
Truths (Sacca)
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements is the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) comprised?
The truth of suffering is comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many is it not comprised?
Nothing is uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements.
The truth of the origin and the truth of the path are each comprised by one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many are they not comprised?
It is not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
The truth of cessation is not included within any aggregates, one base, or one element.
Within how many is it not included?
It is not included within the five aggregates, the eleven bases, or the seventeen elements.
(End of the single-rooted section.
The truth of suffering and the truth of origination are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
The truth of suffering and the truth of the path are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (*khandha*), by any bases (*āyatana*), or by any elements (*dhātu*).

With the exception of the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) as an aggregate, the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) and the truth of cessation (*nirodhasacca*) are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
(The section based on pairs.)
The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, and the truth of the path are comprised within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within any aggregates, nor within any bases, nor within any elements.

The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, and the truth of cessation—excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates—are comprised by the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
(Trikamūlakaṃ.

Suffering-truth, origin-truth, path-truth, and cessation-truth—excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates—are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements.
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are the four truths comprised?
Excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates, the four truths are comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by any elements.
(The Tetrad.)
2.1.5. Faculties (Indriya) By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements is the eye-faculty (cakkhundriya) comprised?
The eye-faculty is comprised by one aggregate, by one base, and by one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
The ear faculty … the nose faculty … the tongue faculty … the body faculty … the female faculty … the male faculty is included by one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
The mind faculty is included by one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
The life-faculty is included by two aggregates, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by three aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
[The same applies to] the faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of mental joy, the faculty of mental grief, and the faculty of equanimity.

… the faculty of faith … the faculty of energy … the faculty of mindfulness … the faculty of concentration … the faculty of wisdom … the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown” … the faculty of final knowledge … the faculty of one who has final knowledge is comprised by one aggregate, by one base, and by one element.
By how many is it not comprised?
It is not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
(End of the section based on one root.
The eye faculty and the ear faculty are included within one aggregate, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The eye faculty and the nose faculty… the eye faculty and the tongue faculty… the eye faculty and [the body faculty]… the eye faculty and…
The body-faculty and … the eye-faculty and the femininity-faculty … the eye-faculty and the masculinity-faculty are included within one aggregate, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The eye faculty and the mind faculty are included within two aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within three aggregates, ten bases, and ten elements.
The eye faculty and the life faculty are included within two aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within three aggregates, ten bases, or sixteen elements.
[This applies to] the eye faculty and the pleasure faculty; the eye faculty and the pain faculty;
the eye faculty and the joy faculty; the eye faculty and the grief faculty; and the eye faculty and the equanimity faculty.

…the faculty of the eye and the faculty of faith … the faculty of the eye and the faculty of energy … the faculty of the eye and the faculty of mindfulness … the faculty of the eye and the faculty of concentration … the faculty of the eye and the faculty of wisdom … the faculty of the eye and the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" … the faculty of the eye and the faculty of final knowledge … the faculty of the eye and…
The faculty of one who has final knowledge is comprised by two aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many is it not comprised?
It is not comprised by three aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
(That which has two roots.
By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are the twenty-two faculties comprised?
The twenty-two faculties are comprised by four aggregates, seven bases, and thirteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), five bases (āyatana), and five elements (dhātu).
2.1.6. Dependent Origination, etc.
Ignorance (avijjā) is included within one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and one element (dhātu).
Within how many is it not included?
It is not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
With ignorance as condition, volitional formations are comprised by one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Consciousness conditioned by volitional formations is included in one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
In how many is it not included?
It is not included in four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
With consciousness as condition, name-and-form is included in four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
In how many is it not included?
It is not included in one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
With name-and-form as condition, the sixfold sense base is comprised by two aggregates, six bases, and twelve elements.
By how many is it not comprised?
It is not comprised by three aggregates, six bases, and six elements.

With the six sense bases as condition, there is contact; with contact as condition, there is feeling; with feeling as condition, there is craving; with craving as condition, there is clinging. Kamma-existence is comprised by one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not comprised?
It is not comprised by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

The existence of rebirth (*upapattibhava*) … the existence of sense-desire (*kāmabhava*) … the existence of perception (*saññābhava*) … the five-aggregate existence (*pañcavokārabhava*) is comprised of five aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
How many is it not comprised of?
It is not comprised of any aggregates; it is not comprised of one base and one element.
Fine-material existence (rūpabhava) is comprised of five aggregates, five bases, and eight elements.
Of how many is it not comprised?
It is not comprised of any aggregates; it is not comprised of seven bases and ten elements.

The formless existence (arūpabhava) … the neither-perception-nor-non-perception existence (nevasaññānāsaññābhava) … the four-aggregate existence (catuvokārabhava) is included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many is it not included?
It is not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Non-percipient existence … and one-aggregate existence are included within one aggregate, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.

Birth is included in two aggregates, in one base, and in one element. In how many is it not included? It is not included in three aggregates, in eleven bases, and in seventeen elements. Aging is included in two aggregates, in one base, and in one element. In how many is it not included? It is not included in three aggregates, in eleven bases, and in seventeen elements. Death is included in two aggregates, in one base, and in one element. In how many is it not included?
It is not included in three aggregates, in eleven bases, and in seventeen elements.
Sorrow … lamentation … pain … grief … despair … the foundation of mindfulness … the right effort is included in one aggregate, in one base, and in one element.
In how many is it not included?
It is not included in four aggregates, in eleven bases, and in seventeen elements.
The basis for spiritual power (iddhipāda) is included within two aggregates (khandha), two bases (āyatana), and two elements (dhātu).
Within how many is it not included?
It is not included within three aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Jhāna is comprised by two aggregates, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not comprised?
It is not comprised by three aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

The immeasurables … the five faculties … the five powers … the seven factors of enlightenment … the noble eightfold path … contact … feeling … perception … volition … resolve … attention are each comprised within one aggregate,
one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Consciousness is included by one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
2.1.7. Triads.
2.1.7.1. The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika) Wholesome phenomena … unwholesome phenomena: by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are they comprised?
Wholesome phenomena … unwholesome phenomena are comprised by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
Indeterminate (abyākata) phenomena—excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the perspective of aggregates—are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
2.1.7.2. The Triplet on Feeling (Vedanāttika)
States associated with pleasant feeling … states associated with painful feeling are included within three aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
States associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are included within three aggregates, two bases, and seven elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, ten bases, and eleven elements.
2.1.7.3. The Triplet of Resultants (Vipākattika).
Resultant states are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
States that are of the nature to ripen as resultants … states that are defiled and subject to defilement are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.

Excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of aggregates, those things which are neither resultant nor productive of resultants are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and thirteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, nor by any bases, but are comprised by five elements.
2.1.7.4. The Triplet of the Clung-to and Subject to Grasping:
Phenomena that are both clung-to and subject to grasping are comprised by five aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, but are included by one base and one element.
Phenomena that are neither-clung-to-nor-liable-to-clinging are included by five aggregates, seven bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandhas), five bases (āyatanas), or ten elements (dhātus).

Phenomena that are neither clung-to nor subject to clinging, and phenomena that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement—excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the perspective of the aggregates—are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
2.1.7.5. The Triplet on the Defiled (Saṅkiliṭṭhattika)
States that are undefiled yet subject to defilement are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not un-included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by any elements.
2.1.7.6. The triad of applied thought:
States with applied thought and sustained thought are included within four aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
States without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states accompanied by rapture, are included in four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
States without applied thought and sustained thought—excluding the unconditioned from the standpoint of aggregates—are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, but are included by one element.
2.1.7.7. The triad of joy:
States accompanied by pleasure are included by three aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
States accompanied by equanimity are included by three aggregates, two bases, and seven elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and eleven elements (dhātu).
2.1.7.8. The Triplet on What is to be Abandoned by Seeing.
States to be abandoned by vision; states to be abandoned by cultivation; states whose roots are to be abandoned by vision;
states whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation; states leading to accumulation; states leading to dispersal;
states of the trainee; states of the adept; and exalted states are included in four aggregates, two bases, and [two elements].
They are included within two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.1.7.9–11. The Triplet of Roots to be Abandoned by Seeing, etc.
States that are neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation; states whose roots are neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation;
states that lead neither to accumulation nor to dispersal; and states that are neither trainee nor beyond-training, namely the unconditioned.
Excluding [the self] from the aggregates, it is included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many is it not included?
It is not un-included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
2.1.7.12. The Triplet of Protective States (Parittattika).
Protective states are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements.
Immeasurable states and sublime states—excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates—are comprised by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.1.7.13. The Triplet of Limited Objects:
Phenomena with limited objects are included in four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
Phenomena having sublime objects … phenomena having immeasurable objects … inferior phenomena … phenomena fixed in falsehood (micchattaniyata) … [are likewise not included].
States that are fixed in rightness, states that have the Path as their object, states that have the Path as their cause,
and states that have the Path as their predominance are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.1.7.14. The Low Triplet:
Middle phenomena are included in five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
2.1.7.15. The Triplet on Wrongness-Determined (Micchattaniyatattika).
The indeterminate states, excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates, are comprised within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within any aggregates, nor within any bases, nor within any elements.
2.1.7.17. The Triplet of the Arisen (Uppannattika) Arisen phenomena are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements.
Unarisen states are comprised by five aggregates, seven bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, five bases, or ten elements.
Phenomena that are subject to arising are comprised by five aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, one base, or one element.
2.1.7.18. The Triplet of the Past:
Past phenomena, future phenomena, present phenomena, internal phenomena, and internal-external phenomena are comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
Excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from among the aggregates, external phenomena are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
2.1.7.19–21. The triad of having past objects, etc.
States with past objects ... states with future objects are included in four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Dhammas with present objects, internal objects, external objects, and both internal and external objects are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
7.22. The Triplet of the Visible.
Phenomena that are visible and impinging are included in one aggregate, in one base, and in one element.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Phenomena that are non-demonstrable and impinging are included within one aggregate, nine bases, and nine elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, three bases, or nine elements.
Excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, phenomena that are non-demonstrable and non-reactive are included within five aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates; they are uncomprised by ten bases and ten elements.
The Group on Causes (Hetugocchaka)

Root-causes (hetu) as phenomena... root-causes that are themselves associated with root-causes (sahetuka)... and root-causes that are themselves associated with root-causes: these are included within one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and one element (dhātu).
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

States that are not roots, states that are rootless, states dissociated from roots, and states that are neither roots nor rootless—excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates—are comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by any elements.
States with roots; states associated with roots; states that have roots but are not themselves roots; states that are associated with roots but are not themselves roots;
and states that are neither roots nor have roots—these are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.1.8.2. The Minor Intermediate Dyads:
Conditioned phenomena ... conditioned phenomena are included in five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, by any bases, nor by any elements.
Unconditioned phenomena (*appaccaya-dhammā*) … unconditioned phenomena (*asaṅkhata-dhammā*) are included by none of the aggregates, by one base, and by one element.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by five aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Visible phenomena (sanidassana-dhammā) are included by one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Non-manifest phenomena—excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates—are included by five aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates; they are not included by one base and one element.
Phenomena with resistance are included by one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Non-reactive phenomena, excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates, are included by five aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates; they are not included by ten bases and ten elements.
Material phenomena are included by one aggregate, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
Immaterial phenomena—excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates—are included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
Mundane phenomena (lokīyā dhammā) are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
Supramundane states—excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates—are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).

Phenomena cognizable by something... phenomena not cognizable by anything: excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the perspective of the aggregates, they are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
2.1.8.3. The Group on the Taints (āsava-gocchaka).

States that are taints (āsava-dhammā) … states that are both taints and objects of the taints (āsava-sāsavā-dhammā) … states that are both taints and associated with the taints (āsava-āsavasampayutta-dhammā) are included within one aggregate, one base, and one element.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

States that are without taints (*anāsava*) ... states dissociated from taints, excluding the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) from the classification of aggregates, are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not unincluded by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.

States with taints (*sāsavā dhammā*) ... states that are both with taints and not themselves taints (*sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā dhammā*) ... states dissociated from taints yet with taints (*āsavavippayuttā sāsavā dhammā*) are included within the five aggregates (*pañca khandhā*), the twelve bases (*dvādasa āyatanāni*), and the eighteen elements (*aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo*).
How many are they not included in?
They are not un-included in any aggregates, nor in any bases, nor in any elements.

States that are without taints (*anāsava*) … states that are dissociated from taints and without taints, excluding the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) from the classification of aggregates, are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.

States associated with the taints (āsava-sampayutta-dhammā) … states that are associated with the taints but are not themselves taints (āsava-sampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā dhammā) are included within four aggregates (khandha), two bases (āyatana), and two elements (dhātu).
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.1.8.4–9. The Group on Fetters (Saṃyojana-gocchaka), etc.
States that are fetters; states that are ties; states that are floods; states that are yokes; states that are hindrances;
states that are adherences; states that are both adherences and the objects of adherence—these are one aggregate, one base, [and one element].
They are included within one element.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

States that are not perversions ... states dissociated from perversions—excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates—are included in five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not unincluded in any aggregates, not unincluded in any bases, and not unincluded in any elements.

States that are adhered to … states that are both adhered to and themselves adhering … states that are dissociated from adhering but are adhered to, are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not un-included in any aggregates, not un-included in any bases, and not un-included in any elements.

States that are unclung-to (*aparāmaṭṭha*) … states that are dissociated from clinging and are unclung-to, excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates, are comprised by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
States associated with misapprehension (parāmāsa) are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.1.8.10. Mahantaraduka:
Phenomena with an object are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Dhammas without an object—excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of aggregates—are included by one aggregate, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
Mental states are included within one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
Non-conscious phenomena (no-citta-dhammā), excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the category of aggregates, are included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.

Mental concomitants (cetasika-dhammā) … states associated with consciousness (cittasampayutta-dhammā) … states conjoined with consciousness (cittasaṃsaṭṭha-dhammā) are included in three aggregates, one base, and one element.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Non-mental factors—excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates—are included by two aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included in three aggregates, nor in any bases, nor in any elements.

Mental states dissociated from consciousness and mental states disconnected from consciousness—excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates—are included in one aggregate, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
Mind-originated states are included within four aggregates, six bases, and six elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, six bases, or twelve elements.

Phenomena not originated by mind … phenomena not co-existent with mind … phenomena not accompanying mind—excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates—are included by two aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included in three aggregates, nor in any bases, nor in any elements.

Mental concomitants that arise simultaneously with consciousness (*cittasahabhū-dhammā*) and mental concomitants that follow after consciousness (*cittānuparivatti-dhammā*) are included in four aggregates, in one base, and in one element.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

Phenomena associated with and produced by consciousness; phenomena that arise together with those associated with and produced by consciousness; and phenomena that follow after those associated with and produced by consciousness: these are included in three aggregates, one base, and one element.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
They are not phenomena associated with and originated by consciousness; they are not phenomena that coexist with those associated with and originated by consciousness;
they are not phenomena that follow upon those associated with and originated by consciousness—excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates, [they are not included] in two...
They are included within the aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by three aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
Internal phenomena are comprised by two aggregates, six bases, and twelve elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by three aggregates, six bases, and six elements.
External phenomena, excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates, are included within four aggregates, six bases, and six elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, six bases, and twelve elements.
Derived phenomena are included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates, all phenomena subject to clinging are included within five aggregates, three bases, and nine elements.
How many are they not included in?
They are not included in any aggregates, nor are they excluded from nine bases and nine elements.
Appropriated phenomena are included within five aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in any aggregates; they are not included in one base and one element.
States not acquired by clinging, excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates, are included in five aggregates, seven bases, and eight elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in any aggregates, in five bases, and in ten elements.
2.1.8.11–12. The Group on Appropriation (Upādāna-gocchaka), etc.
States that are appropriations; states that are defilements; states that are both defilements and subject to defilement; states that are both defilements and defiled;
states that are both defilements and associated with defilements: these are, by way of category, one aggregate and one base.
They are included within one element.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

States that are defilements... states that are not defiled... states that are dissociated from defilements—excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates—are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not unincluded by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.

States that are subject to defilement; states that are both subject to defilement and are themselves defilements; and states that are subject to defilement but dissociated from defilements: these are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not unincluded by any aggregates, not unincluded by any bases, and not unincluded by any elements.

Non-defiled phenomena … non-defiled phenomena dissociated from the defilements—excluding the unconditioned from the standpoint of the aggregates—are included in four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.

Defiled phenomena (*saṅkiliṭṭha-dhammā*), phenomena associated with defilements (*kilesa-sampayutta-dhammā*), phenomena that are both defiled and not themselves defilements (*saṅkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā dhammā*),

and phenomena that are associated with defilements and not themselves defilements (*kilesa-sampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā dhammā*) are included within four aggregates (*khandha*), two bases (*āyatana*), and two elements (*dhātu*).
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.1.8.13. Back-pair:
States to be abandoned by vision; states to be abandoned by cultivation; states whose roots are to be abandoned by vision.
States whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation are comprised by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
States not to be abandoned by vision, states not to be abandoned by cultivation, states whose roots are not to be abandoned by vision,
and states whose roots are not to be abandoned by cultivation— excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates—
are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
Phenomena with applied thought (savitakka) … phenomena with sustained thought (savicāra) are included by four aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements.

States without applied thought (*avitakka*) … states without sustained thought (*avicāra*), setting aside the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) from among the aggregates, are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, but are included by one element.
States accompanied by rapture; states associated with rapture: these are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).

States without rapture (appītika-dhammā) … states not accompanied by rapture (na pītisahagata-dhammā) … states not accompanied by pleasure (na sukhasahagata-dhammā), excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the perspective of aggregates, are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
Phenomena accompanied by pleasure are included by three aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
States associated with equanimity are included by three aggregates, two bases, and seven elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, ten bases, and eleven elements.
States not accompanied by equanimity—excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates—are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and thirteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (*khandha*), nor by any bases (*āyatana*), but they are included by five elements (*dhātu*).

Phenomena belonging to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara-dhamma*) … phenomena that are included (*pariyāpanna-dhamma*) … phenomena that are surpassable (*sauttara-dhamma*) are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, by any bases, or by any elements.

Sensuous-sphere phenomena … non-included phenomena … and unsurpassed phenomena—excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates—are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).

Form-sphere phenomena (rūpāvacara-dhammā) … formless-sphere phenomena (arūpāvacara-dhammā) … leading-out phenomena (niyyānika-dhammā) … fixed-in-fate phenomena (niyata-dhammā) … phenomena with conflict (saraṇa-dhammā) are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).

By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are non-form-sphere states (na rūpāvacarā dhammā) … non-immaterial-sphere states (na arūpāvacarā dhammā) … non-leading-to-deliverance states (aniyyānikā dhammā) … indeterminate states (aniyatā dhammā) … and non-conflict states (araṇā dhammā) included?
The states of non-affliction (araṇā-dhammā), excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates, are comprised within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
The first exposition: the section on the bases of sympathy and non-sympathy.
